_comment: A1 Trading's published Top Setups board, transcribed from their own screen.
This is EVIDENCE, not configuration — nothing reads it at runtime. It exists so
`npm run parity` can score a change against their numbers instead of against an
impression formed by squinting at a browser table.
WHY THIS IS A LIST AND NOT ONE CAPTURE.
Their board is only reachable as frames from their YouTube livestream. A capture
cannot be requested at a chosen moment and cannot be reproduced — whatever the
stream happened to show is all there will ever be of that instant. The previous
shape of this file held exactly one capture and deleted it whenever their board
moved on, which is how the 2026-08-17 cell rows ended up orphaned in
`lib/scoring/edgefinder-parity.test.ts` with no recoverable date. Captures are
append-only now. An old one costs a few hundred bytes; re-taking one is impossible.
`totals` comes from the score column, which is large and unambiguous even in a
compressed video frame. `cells` are the -2..+2 indicator columns, which are not,
and every cell row carries a self-check: the 18 values MUST sum to the row's own
published total. `npm run parity` refuses to attribute a row that fails it. A
WRONG CELL ROW IS WORSE THAN NO CELL ROW, because it explains a gap confidently
and in the wrong direction.
That check is necessary and NOT sufficient — it cannot see two misread cells
that cancel. A row that adds up has earned a test, not belief. The 2026-08-21
note below records a row that passed it and was still wrong, and describes the
second check that caught it.
THERE IS NOW AN EXACT SECOND CHECK, and it runs on every `npm run parity`.
`lib/scoring/a1-legs.ts` treats each captured row as an EQUATION: sixteen of the
eighteen columns are leg-differenced, so a pair cell is `base - quote` over legs
of -1, 0 or +1, and a single-economy row's cell IS one currency's leg. Rows that
each add up individually can still be jointly impossible, and the solver says so
and names the suspects.
IT FIRED IMMEDIATELY ON THE FOUR ROWS BELOW. Every one passes the sum check;
four columns have no solution at all:
Cnsmr Conf       only 2 of 4 rows can hold — two independent contradictions,
CADX/CADCHF and JPYX/GBPJPY. No single row rescues it.
PPI YoY          3 of 4 — re-read CADCHF or CADX
PCE YoY          3 of 4 — re-read GBPJPY or JPYX
Unemploy. Rate   3 of 4 — re-read CADCHF or CADX
So at least four cells in this file are misread, and the per-slot attribution
marks those columns `!! disputed`. DO NOT DRIVE A CONFIG CHANGE OFF THEM.
The columns that DO solve are worth more than the whole rest of the file, because
a pinned leg is a fact about their model and not about the hour the frame was
grabbed — every row was read off one screen at one instant, so the algebra holds
whatever that instant was. It independently reproduces the GBP PPI leg of +1 that
the 2026-08-21 note below reached the long way round, and pins JPY at -1.
THE HIGHEST-VALUE EDIT TO THIS FILE IS STILL A HUMAN-READ ROW, and now it is a
specific one. CADJPY, GBPX and AUDX all have published totals in the newest
capture, and each breaks one of the standoffs above: with CAD and CHF or GBP and
JPY pinned from two directions, a contradiction stops being 'one of these two'
and becomes one named cell with the value it should have carried.
A capture whose provenance is 'unknown' had no recoverable date. It is EXCLUDED
from parity attribution — scoring our board against an undated board measures the
calendar, not the code — but is kept because it still pins date-independent
structure: the composition rule, the +/-2 trend bound, the +/-1 seasonality bound.
Captures are newest first. `scripts/parity.ts` scores against the first one that
has a date.

note: THE FIRST CAPTURE WITH A TIME ON IT, AND THE FIRST WITH A COMPLETE
SINGLE-ECONOMY CELL ROW. Both matter more than the 47 totals.
THE CLOCK. Every capture below is dated to the DAY, so scripts/parity.ts
clamps its rewind to now and scores our board against releases their frame
had never seen. This one carries the timestamp printed on their own Asset
Scorecard header (Aug 23, 2026, 3:11:37 PM UTC), so the rewind lands on the
hour and the comparison is finally like for like.
THE DXY ROW, read off their US-DOLLAR Asset Scorecard, which publishes the
actual and the forecast for every macro row plus four subtotals. It
reconciles seven ways rather than one, which is why it is believed:
technicals      -2 +1                = -1   card prints Technical -1
sentiment+COT   (+1 -1) + 1          = +1   card prints +1
growth          -1 +1 -1 -1 -1       = -3   header Very Bearish
inflation        0 -1  0 -1          = -2   header Bearish
jobs            -1 +1 +1 -1 -1       = -1   header Bearish
fundamentals    -3 -2 -1             = -6   card prints -6
total           -1 +1 -6             = -6   card prints -6
Their published Actual vs Forecast per row, for anyone re-reading the frame:
GDP QoQ 1.50 vs 2.10 | mPMI 55.6 vs 54 | sPMI 54.1 vs 54.5
Retail MoM -0.60 vs 0.10 | Cnsmr Conf 90.8 vs 92.4
NFP -23k vs 85k | Unemp 4.10 vs 4.20 | Claims 206k vs 210k
ADP 44k vs 68k | JOLTS 7.36M vs 7.44M
THEIR RATES ROW IS LABELLED `2 Yr Yield (21 day SMA)` ON THIS CARD, beside a
Bearish cell and a note that the 2yr yield is falling (dovish). That is the
column we fill from the Fed dot plot for an FX leg, and from the 2-year only
for DXY and non-FX assets - see lib/scoring/setups.ts. The two agree today
(the dots project cuts, and the 2-year is under its average), so this is a
latent divergence rather than a live gap. Note also that the rule their card
names is the 2-year against ITS OWN 21-day average, which is NOT the rule
lib/scoring/rates.ts records rejecting: that experiment scored
`yield2y - policyRate`, a level spread that slopes up on every curve and
therefore cancels on every cross. Different rule, different experiment.
TWO PAIR CARDS WERE CAPTURED TOO, AND THEY ARE NOT IN `cells` ON PURPOSE.
Their Forex Scorecard publishes six category gauges and a Bullish, Bearish or
Neutral label per row, but never the signed cell, so a row transcribed from
one would be a guess at magnitude wearing the authority of a number. What
they DO give, differenced against the DXY legs above, is a set of exact
constraints:
EURUSD  total 13  technical 3  COT 2  sentiment 1  growth 5  jobs 0  inflation 2
growth     GDP bull, mPMI neut, sPMI bull, retail neut, cnsmr conf bull
jobs       employment chg bull, unemp bear, claims bear, JOLTS bull, ADP bull
inflation  CPI bull, PPI neut, PCE neut, interest rates bull
NZDUSD  total 7   technical 1  COT 2  sentiment 1  growth 1  jobs 0  inflation 2
growth     GDP bull, mPMI bear, sPMI neut, retail bull, cnsmr conf neut
jobs       employment chg bull, unemp bear, claims bear, JOLTS bull, ADP bull
inflation  CPI bull, PPI neut, PCE neut, interest rates bull
Solved by exhaustive search over every ternary leg assignment, a pair cell
being base minus quote clamped to +/-2, keeping only assignments that match
EVERY published row label AND every category subtotal. Fifteen assignments
survive for each card, so most individual legs are NOT pinned - but the SUM
is identical across all fifteen, which is the quantity the comparison needs:
EUR   pinned      mpmi +1, retail -1, cpi +1, ppi -1, pce 0, rates 0
ambiguous   gdp, spmi, cnsmr conf, nfp, adp, jolts in {0,+1};
unemp, claims in {-1,0}
MACRO LEG SUM = +1, uniquely, under all fifteen.
NZD   pinned      spmi -1, CNSMR CONF -1, cpi +1, ppi -1, pce 0, rates 0
ambiguous   gdp, retail, nfp, adp, jolts in {0,+1};
mpmi, unemp, claims in {-1,0}
MACRO LEG SUM = -3, uniquely, under all fifteen.
The ambiguity is real and worth stating: the algebra permits a euro-area NFP
leg of +1 because a bullish label is satisfied by both 0-(-1) and 1-(-1).
Zero is the sensible reading, but these cards cannot prove it.
AND THAT SETTLES THE EUR HEATMAP QUESTION. Their EURO row reads +7 while our
per-country heatmap reads EUR +1, which looks like a six-point hole. It is
not the same quantity: their 7 is the whole 18-column row, ours is
buildCurrencyHeatmap().macroScore, the economic legs alone. Their own board
says so twice over - EURUSD 13 = EURO 7 minus US-DOLLAR -6, exactly - and the
algebra above puts their EUR macro legs at +1, which is our number.
THE NZD CONSUMER-CONFIDENCE LEG IS THE OPEN QUESTION. Their NZDUSD card reads
that row Neutral while the dollar leg is -1, so the NZD leg must be -1 too:
they have a New Zealand consumer-confidence reading and they score it. The
slot in config/setups.config.ts drops AUD and NZD on the argument that their
per-country heatmap cards carry no such row - which is true, and is exactly
what `matrixOnly: true` on that same slot already records. A card that omits
the column is not evidence that the BOARD column is empty. Do not act on this
from one frame; it is a hypothesis for the leg solver, not a config edit.
COVERAGE. 47 rows map onto our symbol set. AUDX, WTIUSD and the pairs scoring
between +4 and +1 were off-screen between dropdown scrolls and are simply
absent, not zero. No counterpart in our symbol set: CHINA50 (-2), NATGAS (-1).

THE SECOND CAPTURE OF 2026-08-21, AND THE REASON THE FILE NOW SAYS WHY THAT
MATTERS. Taken from the same day's stream a few hours after the one below it.
Their board moved 29 POINTS ACROSS 22 COMPARABLE SYMBOLS between the two, with
16 of the 22 moving at all: CADJPY 10->7, GBPNZD 8->5, DXY -7->-4, GBPUSD 12->10,
GOLD and SILVER both 10->8, EURUSD 8->6, AUDUSD 6->4, USDCHF -9->-7, NZDCAD
-5->-7. TOTAL ABS GAP against this board was 80 at the time, so roughly a third
of the measured gap is WHEN the frame was taken rather than how we score.
That kills the idea that a same-day capture is close enough. The `capturedUtc`
field accepts a full ISO datetime for exactly this reason — record the time
whenever the stream shows it, and parity will rewind to the hour instead of the
day. Without a time the cutoff falls back to end of day clamped to now, which
is what both 2026-08-21 captures use, and is why neither can resolve a gap of
1 to 3 points on any single row.
It also means a row-level fix must clear the timing noise before it counts. Do
not chase a 2-point gap on one symbol; chase a pattern that holds across a
currency's whole set of pairs, or a row like JP-YEN where there is no second
leg to confound it.
US10T has no counterpart in our symbol set. CA-DOLLAR->CADX, US-DOLLAR->DXY,
JP-YEN->JPYX, RUSSELL->RUT2000, NIKKEI->JP225, DAX->GER40, SILVER->XAGUSD,

NO CELLS. A machine transcription of GBPUSD was tried and WITHDRAWN, and how
it failed is the most useful thing recorded in this file.
published total — and was believed on that basis. It read PPI YoY as 0, which
implied our GBP producer-price leg was wrong, so the GBP PPI series was
repointed from core MoM to headline output YoY. That reproduced the 0 exactly
and moved TOTAL ABS GAP from 80 to 90: every sterling pair fell two points
FURTHER from A1 (GBPNZD -5 to -7, GBPJPY -4 to -6, GBPCHF -1 to -3, GBPAUD 0
to -2), and all of them had already been reading low. A1's GBP PPI leg is
therefore +1 and their GBPUSD cell is +2 — the value we already had.
SO THE SUM CHECK IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. It catches a single misread
cell; it cannot catch two that cancel, and 18 cells give it plenty of room. A
row that adds up is a row worth testing, not a row that is right.
The second check is free and much stronger: make the change the cell implies
and run `npm run parity`. A correctly-read cell moves one row toward their
board and leaves the rest alone. A misread one moves a whole currency's pairs
the wrong way, because the leg it points at is shared. Use it before believing
any transcribed row, including a human one.
Adding rows read by a human at full resolution remains the single highest-value
edit to this file.
Taken at a resolution where the score column was legible and the -2..+2 cells
were not, which is why `cells` is empty here and why parity ran blind against
this capture for two days.
US10T has no counterpart in our symbol set. DXY was cut off at the bottom edge
— the bias read 'Very Bearish' but the number did not survive, and a guessed
total would corrupt the one measurement this file exists to provide. GBPCAD and
GBPAUD were neutral, and their board hides neutral rows.
Seven full 18-column rows, rescued from a hard-coded block in
`lib/scoring/edgefinder-parity.test.ts` where they were wired to assertions
about A1's own arithmetic and so could never fail on our code.
THE DATE COULD NOT BE RECOVERED. Git says the block was committed 2026-08-17,
but the rows match neither the totals recorded for 2026-08-17 (GBPUSD 13) nor
the 2026-08-19 capture above (GBPUSD 11, GBPCHF 8, EURUSD 8, NZDUSD 4) — this
capture reads GBPUSD 11, GBPCHF 9, EURUSD 9, NZDUSD 5. They may predate the
repo entirely.
So they are excluded from attribution and kept for what they prove regardless
of date: A1's total is a plain unweighted sum of all 18 columns, trend never
exceeds +/-2, and seasonality never exceeds +/-1 — including on GOLD and
SILVER, where the single-economy path scores macro cells at +/-1 rather than
the +/-2 an FX pair can reach.
GOLD->XAUUSD and SILVER->XAGUSD.
